output.summary: KEP-2943 proposed adding a status subresource to NetworkPolicy objects so that network policy providers could report, as a single Condition (controller, status, description), whether a NetworkPolicy and its features were parsed correctly. The KEP is withdrawn at alpha stage; it was implementable from 2022-02-03 and withdrawn from 2023-01-13.
output.rationale: NetworkPolicy has no status subresource, so providers that fail to parse newer features (for example endPort, SCTP, or port-count limits) cannot tell users that a rule was silently not created. The proposal adds a generic status field so providers can give that feedback. The readme records a drawback: providers may not want the field, since they already expose similar feedback in their own CRDs and the implementation may add overhead.

alternatives.option: Provider-specific validation webhooks that reject invalid NetworkPolicies up front
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists this as an alternative that providers may choose instead of an API field, but it does not say why the KEP did not pursue it.

alternatives.option: Keep feedback in each provider's own CRDs
alternatives.why_not: The readme notes providers already expose this in their CRDs, but it does not say why the generic status field was preferred over that or why the KEP was withdrawn.

evidence.quote: NetworkPolicy objects does not contain a status subresource. This KEP proposes to add this subresource in NetworkPolicy objects
This subresource will contain only a single field with a tuple of (controller, status, description), aka a Condition.
Network Policy Providers may not want to use this field. They already provide this feature as part of their CRDs
Network Policy Providers may want to implement an additional validation webhook instead of relying on an API field
